name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
title: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd - 540699 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Dixon Q2 FY27 revenue INR 21,806 crore; EBITDA ex-fair value gain INR 609 crore, margins squeezed by PLI expiry and memory costs.
summary.overview: Revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR 21,806 crore, with EBITDA of INR 609 crore excluding the fair value gain on the Aditya Infotech stake and PAT after minority interest of INR 293 crore on the same basis. Reported margin percentage fell as mobile PLI 1 expired and elevated global memory prices were passed through to selling prices, which rose roughly 35-40% YoY while volumes were broadly flat. Management reiterated FY27 mobile volume of about 33-34 million excluding Vivo, with Vivo targeted at 55-60 million total, and pointed to new export and Indian-brand customers, plus IT hardware, telecom, display and camera module ramps. Working capital rose in H1 (cash burn of about INR 280 crore per analyst), which management expects to reverse 80-85% before March.

financial_highlights.change: Growth of about 47% YoY per management (Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26)

PAT after minority interest, excl. fair value gain
Consumer electronics (LED TV and refrigerators) revenue

financial_highlights.change: Down from traditional 10.5-11%; about 3% impact in H1 per CFO

financial_highlights.change: As cited by analyst; not disputed by management

segments.name: Mobile and other EMS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 20,093 crore and operating profit INR 509 crore; volumes broadly stable YoY despite India smartphone market down 26% YoY in Q2. H1 volume about 17.2 million; H2 guided at 33-34 million excluding Vivo.

segments.name: Telecom and networking
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,837 crore; microwave backhaul radio production scaled for global brands with exports planned this fiscal. Telecom margin guided at about 3-3.2%.

segments.name: IT hardware
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,160 crore on higher selling prices; current IT hardware margin about 2-2.3% per CFO. Target about INR 6,000 crore revenue this year and INR 15,000-20,000 crore in next couple of years (excludes servers).

segments.name: Home appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 586 crore, operating profit INR 48 crore. Semi-auto washing machine volume up 27% YoY to 6.3 lakh units in Q2 and 16% to 10.9 lakh in H1; FATL volume up 24% to 1.3 lakh in Q2.

segments.name: Consumer electronics (LED TV and refrigerators)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,115 crore, operating profit INR 40 crore; LED TV value and mid-range demand soft, while 50-inch+ and premium QLED/OLED stayed healthy. Plans to move fully to ODM model by Q3.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Described as challenging with subdued demand and pricing pressure; no revenue or margin figure given. Strip-light exports to a large US retail chain have commenced.

guidance_outlook: Mobile volume FY27 about 33-34 million excluding Vivo; with Vivo total about 55-60 million. Q3 volume about 7-7.5 million, Q4 back to about 9.5 million.
Vivo JV (consolidation from Q4): production start targeted Q4 FY27; JV volume about 20-21 million; capex INR 300-350 crore, commercials still being finalised.
Anchor customer (Motorola) MPMS exports to ramp meaningfully from Q4; about 3.5 million units per quarter, of which 6-7 million per year exports; Transsion feature phone exports from next fiscal.

Display and camera modules: display and camera margins to expand 80-100 bps over two years; display capex about INR 1,000 crore over this year, next year and the year after, with revenue potential INR 6,000-7,000 crore.
Q Tech: capacity expanded from 80 million to 120 million, to reach 180-190 million by next fiscal; FY28 revenue target INR 2,500-3,000 crore; margins expected to revert to 6-7% over time.
Capex: about INR 700 crore spent in H1 FY27, about INR 500 crore more in H2, total about INR 1,200 crore this year and INR 1,200-1,300 crore next year.
Working capital: 80-85% of blocked working capital expected to release before March as PLI receivables are realised.
capex_capacity: Washing machine capacity 3.9 million units total (3 million semi-auto, 0.6 million FATL, 0.3 million FLWM), about 33% of estimated 12 million Indian requirement; FLWM launch in Q3 at Tirupati.
Refrigerator capacity to rise from 1.4 million to about 3 million units; facility expansion of about 375,000 sq ft for deep freezers, visi coolers and two-door models.
Noida 1 million sq ft facility almost complete with operations from Q3; Longcheer JV from Q3; Gemtek JV (optical transceivers/BOSA) from Q4 with initial investment INR 50-60 crore under ECMS.

IT hardware: new Inventec JV (60:40) facility in Chennai to start trials in Q3; desktop production from Q3; display line trials by Q3; SSD lines set up. IT PLI commitment raised from INR 250 crore (hybrid) to INR 500 crore (global).
demand_pricing: Selling prices up roughly 35-40% YoY in mobile and IT hardware due to memory cost increase (memory was 12-13% of smartphone BOM, now significantly higher).

Appliances and lighting pass-through lags: EMS segments (mobile, IT, telecom) pass cost through automatically, while washing machines, refrigerators, lighting and part of TV are ODM with time lag. Washing machine margin hit from polymer prices, freight, FX and transit time.
Management says supply of memory is not constrained; cost expected to stay elevated for some time per SK Hynix and Samsung commentary.
Refrigerator industry direct-cool segment declined; Dixon sustained volumes via new brands and side-by-side and multi-door models. Demand for LED TV value/mid-range is soft.

qa_highlights.question: Mobile volumes in Q2 and H2 outlook; export volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 volume about 9.7 million; H1 about 17.2 million; H2 expected 33-34 million excluding Vivo. Anchor customer exports ramp from Q4 with about 3.5 million units per quarter and 6-7 million exports a year; Transsion exports start next fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: IT hardware Rs 15,000-20,000 crore target: does it include servers and what capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Excludes servers; comes from laptops, tablets, desktops. FY27 about 1.3-1.4 million units for INR 6,000-6,500 crore; target 3.5-4 million units at about INR 50-55k per unit, implying INR 20,000-22,000 crore. Server strategy to follow Inventec JV.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact of cost pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Washing machine EBITDA margin compressed to 8.3% from traditional 10.5-11%; H1 impact around 3% for washing machine and a similar figure for lighting, due to polymer prices, freight and FX.

qa_highlights.question: Q Tech margin outlook and FY28 volume ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin dip attributed to FX without pass-through in prior contracts, now partly recovered; capacity expansion and deepening expected to drive operating leverage back to 6-7% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cash burn and reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategic memory inventory, seasonal peak before Q2 and PLI receivables explain build; management expects 80-85% of blocked working capital to release before March.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom and IT hardware margins; ISM 2.0 advanced packaging economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom margin 3-3.2%; IT hardware 2-2.3% now, rising with backward integration (25-30% of BOM) by 80-100 bps. Advanced packaging/silicon photonics ROCE expected close to group level, ASP premium 25-30%.

risks_watch: Smartphone market down 26% YoY in Q2; H2 mobile volume heavily dependent on export ramp-up and Vivo JV start in Q4.
Memory price inflation may persist; pass-through lags in appliances and lighting compress margins (washing machine 8.3%).
Q Tech margins declined about 450 bps in FY26 and H1 revenue flat YoY; recovery to 6-7% is a key watch item.
Execution of multiple new lines (Inventec JV, HKC notebook and mobile lines, Gemtek JV, display, Longcheer) and PLI receivables timing.
MPMS incentive quantum not yet quantifiable; eligibility criteria stricter than earlier expectation per analyst.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and new capability build-out, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term margins, pass-through timing and MPMS incentive quantum, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Margins during the quarter were impacted on expiration of mobile PLI 1 scheme along with elevated global memory prices due to rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

Near-term external headwinds do not alter our medium to long-term growth story, and we continue to see strong opportunities for increasing localization, deepening of manufacturing, new customer additions.

There is a pressure in the market, but I think because of acquisition of our new customers and exports coming into play and our deep stickiness with our existing customers, we are going to grow significantly.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 mobile volume of about 34 million ex-Vivo (H2 33-34 million) and IT hardware revenue of INR 6,000-6,500 crore, backed by Noida, Longcheer, Q Tech and Vivo JV capacity, with the Vivo JV starting production in Q4 (INR 300-350 crore capex), but Q2 margins are squeezed and demand for LED TV is soft.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Washing machine EBITDA margin 8.3% vs traditional 10.5-11% and IT hardware margin 2-2.3%, with pass-through lags; management expects backward integration to add 80-100 bps and Q Tech margin to recover to 6-7%, but memory costs stay elevated and near-term margins were not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Noida 1 million sq ft facility and Longcheer JV from Q3, FLWM launch at Tirupati in Q3, Gemtek JV from Q4, and Vivo JV production start targeted Q4 FY27 with INR 300-350 crore capex; refrigerator capacity rising from 1.4 million to about 3 million units.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Mobile H2 guided at 33-34 million ex-Vivo (H1 about 17.2 million), Q3 Vivo JV 7-7.5 million and Q4 about 9.5 million, plus semi-auto washing machine volume up 27% YoY to 6.3 lakh units in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of about INR 1,200 crore this year and INR 1,200-1,300 crore next year, with display capex about INR 1,000 crore over three years and the IT PLI commitment raised to INR 500 crore, so further commitments are likely as capacity is being built out.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated rather than raised mobile volume (about 34 million ex-Vivo) and IT hardware revenue of INR 6,000-6,500 crore, while Q2 margins were squeezed and MPMS incentive quantum was not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 mobile volume needs 33-34 million ex-Vivo versus 17.2 million in H1 with smartphone market down 26% YoY in Q2, and Vivo JV start is dependent on commercials still being finalised; memory cost pass-through lags could compress margins further.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FLWM washing machine launch at Tirupati in Q3, Transsion feature phone exports from next fiscal, Gemtek optical transceivers (BOSA) from Q4, and Motorola MPMS exports ramping from Q4 at about 3.5 million units per quarter.

rows.label: Motorola MPMS exports ramp and Transsion feature phone exports
rows.why: Anchor customer exports about 3.5 million units per quarter from Q4 (6-7 million per year), with Transsion feature phone exports from next fiscal; MPMS incentive quantum not quantified.

rows.label: Release of blocked working capital
rows.why: Management expects 80-85% of blocked working capital to release as PLI receivables are realised, against an H1 cash burn of about INR 280 crore cited by analyst.

rows.label: IT hardware scale-up to INR 15,000-20,000 crore
rows.why: FY27 IT hardware target INR 6,000-6,500 crore at 1.3-1.4 million units, scaling to 3.5-4 million units; Inventec JV Chennai trials from Q3, but the target excludes servers and margins are 2-2.3%.

tone.note: Management was confident on medium-term growth, new capacity and export ramps, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term margins, pass-through timing and the MPMS incentive quantum; analysts pushed on margin squeeze, working capital burn and the H2 volume dependence.
